items.narrative_markdown:
## Parentage of Patrick Flynn (ca. 1845–1908)

Patrick Flynn is **Probably** the son of Thomas Flynn of Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania.

### Evidence Summary

Three independent lines of evidence support this conclusion:

1. **1850 U.S. Census** (Original Source). Patrick Flynn, age 5, born Ireland, appears in the household of Thomas Flynn, age 32, born Ireland, in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (dwelling 84, family 91). The 1850 census does not state relationships, but Patrick's position in the household and shared surname are consistent with a parent-child relationship. The informant is indeterminate but likely a household member. This constitutes indirect evidence of parentage.

2. **1860 U.S. Census** (Original Source). Patrick Flynn, age 15, born Ireland, appears in the household of Thomas Flynn in Schuylkill County (dwelling 112, family 119). Like the 1850 census, the 1860 census does not state relationships explicitly (the relationship column was not introduced until 1880). Patrick's position in the household, shared surname, and age consistent with the 1850 enumeration support a parent-child relationship. This constitutes indirect evidence of parentage.

3. **1908 Death Certificate** (Original Source). Patrick Flynn's death certificate (no. 4521, Pennsylvania Department of Health) names "Thomas Flynn" as his father. The informant was James Brown, identified as Patrick's son-in-law. As a son-in-law reporting his father-in-law's parentage, Brown is a secondary informant for this fact — he was not a witness to Patrick's birth and is reporting what he was told. Nevertheless, this is direct evidence naming the father.

### Conflict Resolution

A birthplace conflict exists: the 1850 and 1860 censuses list Patrick's birthplace as Ireland, while the 1908 death certificate states Pennsylvania. The two census records are contemporary recordings with informants likely present in the household, while the death certificate was created 63 years after Patrick's birth by a son-in-law with no firsthand knowledge of the event. Per the GPS preponderance hierarchy, contemporary recordings by closer informants outweigh later recollections by secondary informants. Ireland is accepted as the birthplace; the death certificate entry is attributed to informant error.

### Assessment

The conclusion is rated **Probable** rather than **Proved** because: (a) both census sources (1850 and 1860) provide only indirect evidence of parentage (relationships not stated — the relationship column was not introduced until 1880), (b) the death certificate informant is secondary, and (c) research is not yet exhaustive — the 1870, 1880, and 1900 censuses have not been searched, and Thomas Flynn's probate records have not been searched. If Thomas Flynn's will names Patrick as a son, or if additional census records confirm the relationship, the conclusion would advance to **Proved**.

### Citations

1. 1850 U.S. Census, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, population schedule, dwelling 84, family 91, Thomas Flynn household; NARA microfilm publication M432, roll 810; digital image, FamilySearch.org, accessed 1 May 2026.
2. 1860 U.S. Census, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, population schedule, dwelling 112, family 119, Thomas Flynn household; NARA microfilm publication M653, roll 1141; digital image, FamilySearch.org, accessed 2 May 2026.

items.guide_markdown:
## Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania - 1838-1900

Schuylkill County (formed 1811 from Berks and Northampton) lies in Pennsylvania's anthracite coal region. Probate is held by the county Register of Wills from 1811. Catholic parishes moved from the Diocese of Philadelphia to the Diocese of Scranton in 1868. Statewide civil vital registration began only in 1906, so pre-1906 vital events depend on church, cemetery, and probate records. Some coal-region naturalization and church films are browse-only.

entry.rationale: US Census 1880 (FamilySearch collection 1417683, fully indexed, personCount 50,169,452). Unlike earlier census years, 1880 records each person's relationship to the head of household, making it possible to identify by name all children of John Doyle and Bridget Halloran living at home. Highest-priority single source for enumerating the household. Search under head 'John Doyle' or widow 'Bridget Doyle' in Schuylkill County, PA; also search 'Bridget Halloran' in case surname reverted. Name variants: Halloran may appear as Holoran, Haloran, or O'Halloran.

US Census 1870 (FamilySearch collection 1438024, fully indexed, personCount 38,558,371). Captures the household a decade before the 1880 census, when more children would still be living at home. If John Doyle died between 1870 and 1880, this is the last census showing him as head. Also captures children born before 1870 who had left home or died before 1880. Search under 'John Doyle' or 'Bridget Doyle' in Schuylkill County, PA.

US Census 1860 (FamilySearch collection 1473181, fully indexed, personCount 27,518,891). Captures the household twenty years before 1880. Children born before 1860 who died young would appear here and not in later censuses. Also captures older children who had already left home by 1870 or 1880. Search under 'John Doyle' or 'Bridget Doyle' in Schuylkill County, PA.

US Census 1900 (FamilySearch collection 1325221, fully indexed, personCount 76,211,837). Contains a column recording the number of children a mother had borne and the number still living. If Bridget Halloran survives to 1900, this gives a direct count of all her children. Adult Doyle children living independently in Schuylkill County would also appear in their own households. Search under 'Bridget Doyle' or Bridget's later married surname if known, and search adult Doyle children born c.1840-1880 in the county.

FamilySearch collection SYNTH-PA-CHURCH (Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records, personCount 982,415 — fully indexed, dates 1708-1985). As an Irish Catholic immigrant family in the anthracite coal region, the Doyles would have registered baptisms at the local Catholic parish. Each baptismal entry directly names both parents, making this a highly probative source for enumerating all children. Per loc_001, Catholic parishes in Schuylkill County fell under the Diocese of Philadelphia until 1868, then the Diocese of Scranton. Search for baptisms with father 'John Doyle' and mother 'Bridget Halloran' (or Holoran/Haloran variants).

FamilySearch image group 007936751 (Schuylkill County Church Records, 1842-1895, 187 images, 0% indexed — browse only). Per loc_001, some coal-region church films are browse-only and will not appear in the pli_005 name search. Browse register pages for Doyle baptism entries naming John Doyle and Bridget Halloran as parents. This is a fallback for pli_005 and covers registers the indexed collection may not include. Images must be read page-by-page via the search-images skill.

FamilySearch collection 1999196 (Pennsylvania Probate Records, 1683-1994, personCount 0 — browse-only images) and image group 007936749 (Schuylkill County Probate Records, 1851-1930, 412 images, 0% indexed). Per loc_001, probate records are held by the county Register of Wills from 1811. A will or intestate administration for John Doyle would enumerate his heirs — a direct parentage record naming all surviving children at the time of his death. Date range set to John Doyle's plausible lifespan as the creator of the estate: he could have died any time from c.1851 to c.1900. Browse the volume for Doyle entries.

FamilySearch image group 007936753 (Schuylkill County Marriage Records, 1870-1910, 94 images, 0% indexed — browse only). Marriages of Doyle children would record each child's parents' names (John Doyle and Bridget Halloran), providing FAN-cluster cross-references that enumerate the siblings indirectly. Date range covers the period when children born to Bridget c.1840-1865 would reach marriageable age. Browse the volume for any Doyle marriages and note parental names recorded for each. At least one FAN item is required on this completeness question; this item fulfils that requirement.

Ancestry collection 1276 (1850 United States Federal Census, Schuylkill County; URL: https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/). Holds the earliest available indexed census for the period. Children born before 1850 who subsequently died young would appear here and not in any later census. Placed after free FamilySearch searches per 'free before paid' planning principle. Search under head 'John Doyle' or 'Bridget Doyle' in Schuylkill County, PA.

US Census 1910 (FamilySearch collection 1488411, fully indexed, personCount 92,228,496). Captures any surviving Doyle children still in Schuylkill County three decades after the 1880 census. Adult Doyle children who had already left the parental household by 1880 may appear in their own 1910 households. Also indicates whether Bridget is listed as widowed, helping confirm or refine the timeline of John Doyle's death. Search for adult Doyle children born c.1838-1880 in Schuylkill County.

Obituaries for John Doyle or Bridget Halloran in Schuylkill County newspapers typically list all surviving children by name. Chronicling America (https://chroniclingamerica.loc.gov/) holds digitized Pennsylvania newspapers and is a free, full-text-searchable resource. Principal Schuylkill County papers for the period include the Miners' Journal (Pottsville) and the Pottsville Republican. Search for 'John Doyle' and 'Bridget Doyle' or 'Bridget Halloran'. Ancestry newspaper collections serve as a paid fallback if Chronicling America lacks sufficient coverage.

questionStatuses.nextStep: proof-conclusion — resolved with no proof summary

quirks: Schuylkill County was formed in 1811 from Berks and Northampton counties; pre-1811 records are filed under the parent counties.
Probate records (wills, administrations) are held by the county Register of Wills, available from 1811 - a primary parentage source naming heirs.
Roman Catholic parishes fell under the Diocese of Philadelphia until the Diocese of Scranton was erected in 1868; sacramental registers are held at the parish/diocese, not the county.
Pennsylvania statewide civil birth/death registration did not begin until 1906; a 1908 death has a state certificate, but pre-1906 events rely on church, cemetery, and probate records.
Some naturalization and church films for the anthracite coal region are browse-only image groups (volume_search shows ~0% record-searchable) - browse image-by-image.

entry.rationale: Patrick's 1908 Pennsylvania death certificate is the most direct available evidence for q_001 — PA death certificates of this era name the deceased's parents. S3 in tree.gedcomx.json (cert. no. 4521) is already attached to the parent-child relationship R1 (quality 2) and to Patrick's death fact (F2), but has no corresponding research.json source entry and no extracted assertions; its stated parentage content is therefore unknown to the research workflow. FamilySearch collection 2255317 (Pennsylvania Death Certificates, 1906–1968; personCount 4,218,763) is indexed and name-searchable. Searching for Patrick Flynn d. 1908 will confirm this certificate and allow proper extraction of parentage assertions. Search here first — if the certificate names both parents, it may answer q_001 outright and sharply focus remaining searches.

S2 in tree.gedcomx.json (1860 Census, dwelling 112, Schuylkill Co.) is already attached to parent-child relationship R1 but has no research.json source entry and no extracted assertions. FamilySearch collection 1473181 (United States Census, 1860; personCount 27,518,891) is indexed. Patrick (~15 in 1860) in Thomas Flynn's household for a second consecutive census strengthens the inferred co-residency beyond a single snapshot. The 1860 census does not state family relationships, so this remains indirect evidence; however, two census appearances together are substantially stronger than one. Also search for Thomas Flynn to note any other household members (e.g., a wife who would be Patrick's mother). Use variant spellings Flynn/Flyn/Flinn.

The 1880 US census was the first to explicitly state family relationships for every household member. If Thomas Flynn (b. ~1818, ~62 in 1880) is still alive and residing in Schuylkill County, his wife would appear with relationship 'wife' — directly naming Patrick's mother. FamilySearch collection 1417683 (United States Census, 1880; personCount 50,169,452) is indexed. Search both Thomas Flynn (b. ~1818, Ireland) for his wife's name and Patrick Flynn (b. ~1845) in his own household — the 1880 census also records each person's mother's and father's birthplace, which may corroborate Irish origin. Use variants Flynn/Flyn/Flinn.

The 1900 US census was the first to ask respondents for their father's and mother's birthplace — entries for Patrick Flynn (b. ~1845, ~55 in 1900) and, if still living, Thomas (b. ~1818, ~82) would directly record those birthplaces, corroborating the Ireland origin noted on Thomas's tree fact (F3). FamilySearch collection 1325221 (United States Census, 1900; personCount 76,211,837) is indexed. Patrick died 1908-03-12 so he was alive in June 1900; search for him in Schuylkill County. Use variants Flynn/Flyn/Flinn.

Patrick's baptismal record (~1845) would directly name his father and mother — the highest quality direct parentage evidence and the strongest corroboration for any name obtained from the death certificate. loc_001 notes Catholic parishes in the Schuylkill County anthracite region fell under the Diocese of Philadelphia until 1868 and that sacramental registers are held at the parish or diocese. FamilySearch collection SYNTH-PA-CHURCH (Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records, 1708–1985; personCount 982,415) is indexed and name-searchable; search for Patrick Flynn b. ~1845. Note: tree fact F1 records Patrick's birth place as Ireland (sourced to S1, the 1850 census) while the project objective states Pennsylvania — if born in Ireland, a baptism would not appear in this collection, but the census birthplace should be resolved during extraction. Use variants Flynn/Flyn/Flinn. If the indexed collection does not return the baptism, see pli_013 (church browse fallback).

Parentage questions require a dedicated search for the candidate parents' marriage to each other. Thomas Flynn (I2, b. ~1818, Ireland) is the candidate father; his wife — Patrick's mother — is entirely absent from the tree and from all extracted assertions. A marriage record for Thomas would name his wife and establish her identity. Search FamilySearch indexed collections: SYNTH-PA-CHURCH (Schuylkill County Church Records, personCount 982,415), collection 1571957 (Pennsylvania Civil Marriages, 1677–1950; personCount 624,090), and collection 1502909 (Pennsylvania Compiled Marriages, 1700–1900; personCount 397,530). Date range set by Patrick's birth ~1845 — Thomas and his wife likely married in the early-to-mid 1840s. Caution: the marriage record names Thomas's wife as she was at that marriage — if she had a prior marriage, that surname is not her birth name, and additional searches for her earlier marriage and her own parents would be needed. If indexed collections yield nothing, see pli_013 (church browse vol. 007936751) which covers 1842–1895 and may hold the church register entry.

The 1870 census bridges the gap between the 1860 and 1880 enumerations. By 1870 Patrick (~25) may have left Thomas's household, but Thomas (~52) with a wife would fill a gap in the residency timeline and may supply a wife's name (though 1870 does not state relationships). FamilySearch collection 1438024 (United States Census, 1870; personCount 38,558,371) is indexed. Search for both Thomas Flynn and Patrick Flynn in Schuylkill County. Use variants Flynn/Flyn/Flinn.

Thomas Flynn's will or letters of administration would name his heirs — which should include Patrick — providing direct stated parentage evidence independent of the census inferences. loc_001 confirms probate records are held by the Schuylkill County Register of Wills (available from 1811). FamilySearch collection 1999196 (Pennsylvania Probate Records, 1683–1994; personCount 0) and volume 007936749 (Schuylkill County Probate Records, 1851–1930; imageCount 412, recordSearchablePercent 0%) are both browse-only image groups — no name search is possible; page-by-page image browse required. S4 (Schuylkill County Probate Records) is already in tree.gedcomx.json as a source description but is not linked to any person or fact, suggesting a prior researcher anticipated this source. Date range is set by Thomas's plausible death years: he appears in the 1850 census (age ~32, b. ~1818) and may have died any time through the early 1900s — the window is bounded by Thomas's plausible lifespan, not capped at Patrick's 1908 death.

FAN item: Thomas Flynn (b. ~1818, Ireland) is the candidate father — his own records bear on Patrick's parentage. Declarations of intention (first papers) filed by Irish immigrants in the Schuylkill County coal region in the 1850s–1860s sometimes named the applicant's wife and children, which would directly corroborate the Thomas-Patrick relationship and potentially name Patrick's mother. Volume 007936750 (Schuylkill County Naturalization Records, 1849–1915; imageCount 298, recordSearchablePercent 0%) is browse-only — page-by-page browse required. Date range capped at 1880 as Thomas (b. ~1818) would very likely have naturalized before then. Use variants Flynn/Flyn/Flinn.

Browse-only fallback for pli_008 (Patrick's baptism) and pli_009 (Thomas's marriage) if neither indexed search returns a result. Volume 007936751 (Schuylkill County Church Records, 1842–1895; imageCount 187, recordSearchablePercent 0%, languages en/de) is a browse-only image group covering the target period for both searches. Browse page-by-page through pages ca. 1842–1855 for Thomas Flynn's marriage entry and ca. 1843–1848 for Patrick Flynn's baptism. loc_001 notes some films for the anthracite coal region are browse-only, and this volume is one of them.
